text:
maya: heads up — sales flagged a Tier-1 merchant that will only go live if we match CompetitorX's routing controls. they want per-tenant routing rules (+ UI) and an A/B fallback in case of overload. do we: ship a lightweight parity shim fast, or prioritize a durable differentiator path that buys us better economics later? cc @jordan @samir
jordan: what's the minimal acceptance? last time 'parity' meant they only cared about the API surface, not exact UX.
samir: sales sent a note — they want: API parity + simple rule UI by pilot launch date (6 weeks). They called out: per-tenant route weights, priority tiers, and a manual failover toggle.
elaine: timeline is tight — 6 weeks is doable only if we scope to a thin shim (no full rollout controls or console polish). can we reuse the tenant-routing prototype from the spike?
alex: reuse seems realistic. tradeoffs: shim = faster revenue but duplicate tech debt; full solution = longer runway for other customers. recommend: ship shim + tech-debt ticket + short lifecycle (30d) to migrate rules to canonical config.
maya: agreed. we need clear launch criteria tho. propose: 1) API parity for route selection, 2) end-to-end latency impact under 99th pctl +15ms, 3) no regression on per-route SLOs, 4) console minimal (toggle + list), 5) telemetry that shows fallback rates.
jordan: add must-have: canary flag so we can flip back to global routing. and a kill-switch in case we see error spike.
samir: ops ask: include a dashboard widget showing route utilization and fallback counts. also an alert if fallback > 5% sustained for 10m.
elaine: ok — implementation plan: week 1: adaptor layer + API endpoints; week 2: basic UI and canary; week 3: telemetry + alerts; week 4: pilot hardening + customer onboarding. 
alex: can we compress: parallelize UI and adaptor work, need one extra FE person for week 2-3. otherwise scope creep will push beyond 6w.
maya: resource ask noted. @eng-leads — can we allocate an FE contractor for 3 sprints? otherwise we say no-go and offer a limited API-only pilot.
jordan: product decision: do we document this as "parity shim (temporary)" in the roadmap or surface as feature? I vote roadmap: "Pilot: parity shim — Q2" with follow-up project "Canonical routing controls". keeps expectations clear.
samir: Sales message to customer should state: pilot meets their immediate API requirements; full console/advanced routing scheduled for H2. must capture acceptance test cases.
elaine: quick acceptance checklist suggestion: POST /routes accepts weight/rank, GET /routes returns tenant rules, UI shows toggle and history (last 24h). sample CLI to test:
```
# create weighted rule
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"tenant":"acme","rules":[{"variant":"v2","weight":80},{"variant":"v1","weight":20}]}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/tenants/acme/routes
```
alex: good. also add an automated smoke test that runs this script and asserts fallback rate zero on green cluster.
maya: decision: ship parity shim with canary + telemetry + explicit deprecation window (30d) to migrate. product will log a follow-up epic for canonical routing (scope: RBAC, advanced schedules, UI rule composer).
jordan::+1: add to roadmap and sync with sales messaging including migration SLA.
samir: i'll draft the sales acceptance doc and share later today.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: feature/parity-shim -> staging at 2026-05-04T09:30Z (baseline).
elaine: thx everyone. i'll open the pilot PRD and link acceptance checklist. we should reconvene Thurs for resource confirmation.
